source_text: XIX. Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἦλθεν ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἰς τὴν Σμύρναν, καὶ προσαχθεὶς ὁ Πιόνιος ἐμαρτύρησε, γενομένων ὑπομνημάτων τῶν ἐπιτεταγμένων, πρὸ τεσσάρων εἰδῶν Μαρτίων. καθεσθεὶς πρὸ βήματος Κυντιλλιανὸς ἀνθύπατος ἐπηρώτησε· Τίς λέγῃ; ἀπεκρίθη· Πιόνιος. ὁ δὲ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Ἐπιθύεις; ἀπεκρίνατο· Οὔ. ὁ ἀνθύπατος ἐπηρώτησεν· Ποίαν θρησκείαν ἢ αἵρεσιν ἔχεις; ἀπεκρίνατο· Τῶν καθολικῶν. ἐπηρώτησε· Ποίων καθολικῶν; ἀπεκρίνατο· Τῆς καθολικῆς ἐκκλησίας εἰμὶ πρεσβύτερος. ἀνθύπατος· Σὺ εἶ ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτῶν; ἀπεκρίνατο· Ναί, ἐδίδασκον. ἐπηρώτησε· Τῆς μωρίας διδάσκαλος ἦς; ἀπεκρίθη· Τῆς θεοσεβείας. ἐπηρώτησε· Ποίας θεοσεβείας; ἀπεκρίθη· Τῆς [sic] εἰς τὸν θεὸν πατέρα τὸν ποιήσαντα τὰ πάντα. ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Θῦσον. ἀπεκρίνατο· Οὔ· τῷ γὰρ θεῷ εὔχεσθαί με δεῖ. ὁ δὲ λέγει· Πάντες τοὺς θεοὺς σέβομεν καὶ τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τοὺς ὄντας ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ θεούς. τί τῷ ἀέρι προσέχεις; θῦσον αὐτῷ. ἀπεκρίθη· Οὐ τῷ ἀέρι προσέχω ἀλλὰ τῷ ποιήσαντι τὸν ἀέρα καὶ τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς. ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Εἶπον, τίς ἐποίησεν; ἀπεκρίνατο· Οὐκ ἔξεστιν εἰπεῖν. ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Πάντως ὁ θεός, τουτέστιν ὁ Ζεύς, ὅς ἐστιν ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, βασιλεὺς γὰρ πάντων τῶν θεῶν. XX. Σιωπῶντι δὲ τῷ Πιονίῳ καὶ κρεμασθέντι ἐλέχθη· Θύεις; ἀπεκρίνατο· Οὔ. πάλιν βασανισθέντι αὐτῷ ὄνυξιν ἐλέχθη· Μετανόησον. διὰ τί ἀπονενόησαι; ἀπεκρίνατο· Οὐκ ἀπονενόημαι ἀλλὰ ζῶντα θεὸν φοβοῦμαι. ὁ δὲ ἀνθύπατος· Ἄλλοι πολλοὶ ἔθυσαν καὶ ζῶσι καὶ σωφρονοῦσιν. ἀπεκρίνατο· Οὐ[--- — reply tail lost in scan]. ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Ἐπερωτηθεὶς λόγισαί τι παρὰ σεαυτῷ καὶ μετανόησον. ἀπεκρίνατο· Οὔ. ἐλέχθη αὐτῷ· Τί σπεύδεις ἐπὶ τὸν θάνατον; ἀπεκρίνατο· Οὐκ ἐπὶ τὸν θάνατον ἀλλ᾽ ἐπὶ τὴν ζωήν. Κυντιλλιανὸς ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Οὐ μέγα πρᾶγμα ποιεῖς σπεύδων ἐπὶ τὸν θάνατον· καὶ γὰρ οἱ ἀπογραφόμενοι ἐλαχίστου ἀργυρίου πρὸς τὰ θηρία θανάτου καταφρονοῦσι, καὶ σὺ εἷς ἐκείνων εἶ· ἐπεὶ οὖν σπεύδεις ἐπὶ τὸν θάνατον ζῶν κατακαήσῃ. καὶ ἀπὸ πινακίδος ἀνεγνώσθη Ῥωμαϊστί· Πιόνιον ἑαυτὸν ὁμολογήσαντα εἶναι Χριστιανὸν ζῶντα κατακαῦσαι προσετάξαμεν.
pass_a_gloss: After these things the proconsul came to Smyrna, and Pionius when brought forward bore witness, with official minutes of the orders having been made, four days before the Ides of March. Quintillian the proconsul, seated before the tribunal, asked 'What are you called?' He answered 'Pionius.' The proconsul said 'Do you sacrifice?' He answered back 'No.' The proconsul asked 'What religion or sect do you have?' He answered 'Of the catholics.' He asked 'Of what catholics?' He answered 'I am a presbyter of the catholic church.' Proconsul: 'Are you their teacher?' He answered 'Yes, I was teaching.' He asked 'Were you a teacher of folly?' He answered 'Of godliness.' He asked 'Of what godliness?' He answered '[extraneous] toward God the Father who made all things.' The proconsul said 'Sacrifice.' He answered 'No, for I must pray to God.' And he says 'We all revere the gods and heaven and the gods being in heaven; why do you attend to air? Sacrifice to it.' He answered 'I do not attend to air but to the one who made the air and heaven and all the things in them.' The proconsul said 'Tell, who made?' He answered 'It is not permitted to say.' The proconsul said 'Certainly god, that is Zeus, who is in heaven, for he is king of all the gods.' To Pionius while silent and hung up it was said 'Do you sacrifice?' He answered 'No.' When he was again tortured with claws it was said 'Repent; why have you become senseless?' He answered 'I have not become senseless but I fear a living God.' And the proconsul: 'Many others sacrificed and live and are of sound mind.' He answered 'No—' with the rest of the reply lost by break. The proconsul said 'When questioned reckon something with yourself and repent.' He answered 'No.' It was said to him 'Why do you hasten to death?' He answered 'Not to death but to life.' Quintillian the proconsul said 'You do no great thing hastening to death; for even those enrolled for very little money despise death before the beasts, and you are one of those; since then you hasten to death, you shall be burned alive.' And from a tablet it was read in Latin: 'We ordered Pionius, who confessed himself to be a Christian, to be burned alive.'
pass_b_english: After these things the proconsul came to Smyrna, and Pionius was brought forward and bore his witness, with the official record of the orders made, four days before the Ides of March.
Quintilianus the proconsul took his seat before the tribunal and asked, Who are you called?
He answered, Pionius.
The proconsul said, Will you sacrifice?
He replied, No.
The proconsul asked, What observance or sect do you hold?
He replied, That of the catholics.
He asked, Which catholics?
He replied, I am a presbyter of the catholic church.
The proconsul said, Are you their teacher?
He replied, Yes, I was teaching.
He asked, Were you a teacher of folly?
He answered, Of reverence for God.
He asked, Of what reverence for God?
He answered, That toward God the Father who made all things.
The proconsul said, Sacrifice.
He replied, No, for I must pray to God.
He said, We all revere the gods, and heaven, and the gods who are in heaven.
Why do you heed the air?
Sacrifice to it.
He replied, I do not heed the air, but the one who made the air and heaven and all things in them.
The proconsul said, Tell me, who made them?
He replied, It is not permitted to say.
The proconsul said, Surely it is god, that is Zeus, who is in heaven, for he is king of all the gods.
While Pionius kept silence and was hung up, he was asked, Will you sacrifice?
He answered, No.
When he was tortured again with the claws, he was told, Repent.
Why have you lost your senses?
He answered, I have not lost my senses, but I fear the living God.
The proconsul said, Many others have sacrificed, and they live and are sound of mind.
He answered, No, and the rest of the reply is lost.
The proconsul said, Now that you are questioned, reckon with yourself and repent.
He answered, No.
He was told, Why do you hasten to death?
He answered, Not to death, but to life.
Quintilianus the proconsul said, You do no great thing in hastening to death, for even men enrolled for the smallest sum despise death before the beasts, and you are one of them.
Since then you hasten to death, you shall be burned alive.
And from the tablet the sentence was read in Latin: We have ordered that Pionius, who has confessed himself to be a Christian, be burned alive.

lemmas.gloss: bore witness, made confession under trial
to pray, here duty to pray to God
to burn alive, consume by fire

choices.why: aorist of witness-speech in a trial with minutes; not yet the death itself, which is sentenced later

choices.english: What observance or sect do you hold
choices.why: pair asks for affiliation; θρησκεία is outward observance and αἵρεσις is party/school, so both kept

choices.english: become senseless / I have not lost my senses
choices.why: perfect of mind-failure in reproach and denial; moral folly charge answered by fear of God
